name: Geometric Selection Conjecture: the mirror-fixed clause of Theorem D is empty, so GSC is equivalent to a viable vacuum outside L^mu (partial result)
target: Theorem 22 of creelie/strings (Hexagon 2610.00446v1): GSC holds iff a viable vacuum V* exists with mu(V*) = V* whenever V* lies in L^mu
result: Proved by hand: a mu-fixed vacuum of L^mu is isomorphic to its mirror, so chi(X) = 0, c_3(V) = 0 on its standard-type component and the index chi(X, V) = c_3/2 vanishes, so it has no net families and fails (C2). Hence GSC is equivalent to the existence of a viable vacuum on a component carrying no standard embedding, and no standard embedding is ever selected; the existence statement stays open.

notes.formal: no Lean statement; the proof is three steps of Hodge theory and Hirzebruch-Riemann-Roch
notes.sim: no simulation applies; the lemma and the corollary are checked on Hodge data in construct/gsc_mirror_fixed.py
notes.human: the note (5 pages) is prepared for a letters journal and not refereed
notes.lit: literature check of 21 October 2026: no published heterotic model establishes (C7), (C8) and (C9) together, so the existence statement is not closable from the literature
